title: The Euclidean plane cannot be colored with five colors

result.label: The Euclidean plane cannot be colored with five colors
result.statement: Proves that every five-coloring of the Euclidean plane has a monochromatic pair at distance one, with no restriction on the color classes. This advances the Hadwiger–Nelson problem: together with the classical seven-coloring, only six and seven remain possible chromatic numbers of the plane.
